Issued at 254 PM EDT Tue Sep 29 2026

Now through Wednesday Night...

Afternoon observations reveal mostly sunny skies across the region 
with temperatures in the upper 70s.  A few 80 degree readings were 
noted in the I-65 corridor and points west.  No significant weather 
is expected through the remainder of the afternoon and into the 
evening hours.  Afternoon highs will top out in the upper 70s to the 
lower 80s.  Upper ridging and surface high pressure will continue to 
strongly control our weather overnight.  Mostly clear skies and light 
southeast winds are expected.  We could see some valley fog with 
overnight lows in the mid-upper 50s.

Upper level ridging will hold sway across the southeastern US on 
Wednesday.  We may have some very high cirrus streaming across 
western portions of the region.  A surface area of high pressure 
will be located to our east and we'll have a south to southwest flow 
in the region.  This should allow temperatures to warm up a bit more 
over what we saw on Tuesday.  Highs of 80-85 are expected across our 
northeast areas, but we'll see mid-upper 80s in the I-65 corridor. 
Upper 80s will be possible across our far southwest (Bowling Green) 
area.  Latest HREF probabilities of 90 degrees are pretty low across 
our region (<10%) and more likely to be seen in area west of I-165. 
Dry weather will continue Wednesday night with lows in the 60-65 
degree range.

Thursday through Monday...

Upper ridge axis looks to hold on strong for Thursday with a 
continued southwest flow at the surface.  Under partly to mostly 
sunny skies, we'll see temperatures flex into the upper 80s.  Best 
chances of hitting 90, look to be west of I-65 where the NBM blend 
probabilities stand at greater than 60 percent, with 80-90% at 
Bowling Green.  90s still seem unlikely over at Lexington as the 
blend only gives about a 30% probability of exceeding 90.  However, 
in deep southwest/warm advection cases, the models usually are too 
cool with highs. 

By Thursday night, a slow moving upper level trough axis and surface 
cold front will slowly push into the region from the west. 
Widespread showers are likely after midnight Thursday night and will 
continue into the day on Friday as the frontal boundary slowly 
pushes through the region.  Looking at model proximity soundings, 
the widespread cloudiness and ongoing precipitation will likely 
limit our instability.  Wind shear values are also weak below 8km. 
Lapse rates are not all that steep in the low-mid levels, so it may 
be hard to even get some lightning out of the activity.  The model 
soundings do have plentiful moisture as PWATs are up over 2 inches. 
So locally heavy rainfall will be possible across the region. 
However, the recent stretch of dry weather across much of the CWA 
should preclude any hydro issues.  Highs on Friday look to feature a 
gradient with the front in the area.  Highs may struggle to get into 
the low-mid 70s in areas north of the Ohio River, with low-mid 80s 
across much of Kentucky.

Latest 12Z guidance looks a bit more optimistic for drier conditions 
on Saturday as the models are a little faster with pushing the front 
south of the region.  29/13Z Blend is probably too high here as the 
00/06Z were slower, so I expect that we'll trend down PoPs in later 
forecasts.  For now, the best chances of any residual rain showers 
looks confined to mainly southern KY for Saturday and into the day 
on Sunday.  Highs on Saturday will feature a gradient as well with 
upper 60s to around 70 in southern Indiana and far northern 
Kentucky.  Lower 70s are expected in areas south of the WK/BG 
Parkway.  Similar readings are expected on Sunday with highs just a 
few degrees either side of 70.  Lows through the period will be 
in the low-mid 50s.  

Drier and much cooler air will arrive for Monday with highs likely 
topping out in the upper 60s over much of the region.  A few 
readings near 70 will be possible down along the KY/TN border.  Lows 
Monday night will be the coolest of the forecast period with lows in 
the upper 30s to the lower 40s in the north with mid 40s in the 
south.  Depending on cloud cover and wind forecasts, some patchy 
frost could be possible in our northern and most protected areas.
